front_matter.title: The joint Clifford clause (f) is a Klein convention on the composite space
front_matter.subject: standard-model

extraction.note: Answers whether clause (f) of the slot-module hypothesis (slots and pairs one Clifford system) adds content on the composite space V = F (x) Lambda W: it does not. On V the natural slot operators commute with the pair operators; their Klein twists a (-1)^k anticommute with them, obey the same CAR, covariance and generation, and are unique up to a unit (sign, for an involution); the split-preserving (Pati-Salam) bivectors and the grading are the same operators in both conventions. Realised in the floor Cl(5,5) of synthesis.even-slots-need-a-spectator-generator, where the pair parity is the single blade e2 f2 e3 f3 e4 f4 (1 - 2 v w = e f), so uniqueness is a count with the commutation form of synthesis.blade-square-signs-f2-quadratic-form. The Majorana generator of square -1 is a real vector f_k, so no imaginary unit is needed; numbers are read in span{1, I4}. Pre-registered kill condition: a result in the future cone of (f) whose statement changes beyond an overall sign under a -> a (-1)^k, that is, one using the slot operators as given tower elements. Not run over the whole future cone; the clause keeps content exactly in that embedded reading, which this result does not address. The Klein transformation itself is standard (O. Klein 1938; H. Araki 1961; cited from memory), reproved here. Transport-absent.
flags: the kill condition was not run over the future cone of the slot-module hypothesis: results that use the slot operators as given tower elements could still give clause (f) content; on V itself it has none

levels.formal:
Read numbers in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$. Let $V = F \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W$ be the composite space of Premise \claimref{standard-model.slot-module-hypothesis}(a) with fermionic slot module $F = \Lambda^{\bullet}D$, $D$ the slot doublet; let $a_{i} = a(u_{i}) \otimes 1$ ($i = 1, 2$) be the slot annihilators, $b_{p} = 1 \otimes b(t_{p})$ ($p = 1, 2, 3$) the pair annihilators, $(-1)^{k}$ the pair parity, $(-1)^{N} = (-1)^{n + k}$ the grading, and $\tilde a_{i} = a_{i}(-1)^{k}$ the Klein-twisted slot operators.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] \emph{(Same slot data; proved.)} The $\tilde a_{i}$ satisfy the same canonical anticommutation relations as the $a_{i}$, transform in the same way under $U(2) \times U(3)$, and on $F_{n} \otimes \Lambda^{k}W$ have $\tilde a_{i}^{\dagger} = (-1)^{k}a_{i}^{\dagger}$, so clause (G) holds for one set exactly when it holds for the other.
\item[(ii)] \emph{(Opposite relation to the pairs; proved.)} The $a_{i}$ commute with every $b_{p}$, $b_{p}^{\dagger}$; the $\tilde a_{i}$ anticommute with them. So $\tilde a_{1}, \tilde a_{2}, b_{1}, b_{2}, b_{3}$ satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations of one system of five modes, and their real Majorana combinations, five of square $+1$ and five of square $-1$, generate $\Cl(5,5)$ on $V$, whose span over $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$ is the $\Cl(10)$ of clause (f).
\item[(iii)] \emph{(Convention-free operators; proved.)} The $21$ split-preserving bivectors (the $6$ slot-slot and $15$ pair-pair Majorana bivectors, the Pati-Salam algebra of clause (CPT)) and the grading $(-1)^{N}$, which anticommutes with $a_{i}$, $\tilde a_{i}$ and $b_{p}$ alike, are the same operators in both conventions.
\item[(iv)] \emph{(Uniqueness; proved.)} If an operator $K$ on $V$ commutes with every $a_{i}$, $a_{i}^{\dagger}$ and the $a_{i}K$ anticommute with every pair operator and satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations, then $K = c(-1)^{k}$ with $c$ a unit of $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$ (a phase from the centre of the slot $U(2)$), and $c = \pm 1$ if $K$ is an involution.
\item[(v)] \emph{(Consequence; proved on $V$.)} Clause (f) holds on $V$ for every $F \cong \Lambda^{\bullet}D$, canonically up to that unit: it is a convention on $V$ (the $24$ cross bivectors depend on the convention, but the residual sign acts on them by $\mathrm{Ad}$ of the slot parity, an element of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$, so the $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ of clause (f) is canonical), and the qualifier of clause (CPT) ``when the slot module is fermionic, so that clause (f) applies'' adds no condition beyond $F \cong \Lambda^{\bullet}D$. The clause keeps content only relative to slot operators given in advance, for instance as tower elements (the setting of \claimref{synthesis.even-slots-need-a-spectator-generator}(iii)), which is not addressed.
\end{enumerate}
The twist is the replacement $s_{i} \mapsto s_{i}\Gamma_{W}$ of \claimref{synthesis.even-slots-need-a-spectator-generator}(iii), the commuting-copies device of \claimref{tower.commuting-copies} read backwards. In the floor $\Cl(5,5)$ of \claimref{synthesis.even-slots-need-a-spectator-generator}, with the modes as null pairs of vectors, the twisted operators are the vectors themselves, the untwisted ones are the vectors times the pair parity $\Gamma_{W} = e_{2}f_{2}e_{3}f_{3}e_{4}f_{4}$, a single blade, and (iv) is a count of blades with the commutation form of \claimref{synthesis.blade-square-signs-f2-quadratic-form}(ii). Transport-absent.
levels.technical: Clause (f) of the slot-module hypothesis asks that the slot and pair operators of a composite form one system of five fermionic modes, each slot operator anticommuting with each pair operator. On the tensor-product space $V = F \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W$ the natural slot operators commute with the pair operators instead. Multiplying them by the pair parity $(-1)^{k}$, the Klein transformation, turns commuting into anticommuting while keeping their anticommutation relations, their $U(2) \times U(3)$ behaviour and their images, so generation is unaffected. Everything the hypothesis asks of the chirality is the same in both conventions: the slot-slot and pair-pair bivectors (the Pati-Salam algebra) and the grading by the total mode number. The twist is unique: a factor commuting with the slot operators and making them anticommute with the pairs is a unit times $(-1)^{k}$, because it then commutes with all operators on $V$. In geometric algebra the five modes are null pairs of vectors in $\Cl(5,5)$, the twisted slot operators are those vectors, and the pair parity is the single blade $e_{2}f_{2}e_{3}f_{3}e_{4}f_{4}$; uniqueness is then a count with the two-element-field commutation form of blades. So on $V$ clause (f) is a convention, not a premise; it would carry content only for slot operators fixed in advance, for instance as tower elements, which this result does not treat. Transport-absent.
levels.lay: The series builds each quark or lepton from two kinds of ingredients, slots and pairs, and one of its assumptions says that the two kinds behave as a single family of fermions, swapping sign whenever one of each is exchanged. This result shows that, on the particle's own space of states, this costs nothing: if slot and pair operators are first written so that they ignore each other, a standard trick (multiplying each slot operator by a sign that counts the pairs) makes them behave as one family, changes nothing else that the theory uses, and is the only way to do it up to an overall sign. The assumption only matters if the slot operators are fixed in advance by something else, such as the deeper tower of the theory.
levels.one-liner: On the composite space $V = \Lambda^{\bullet}D \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W$ the Klein-twisted slot operators $a(-1)^{k}$ keep the slot CAR, covariance and generation, anticommute with the pair operators where the untwisted ones commute, leave the $21$ Pati-Salam bivectors and the grading unchanged, and are unique up to a unit, so clause (f) is a convention on $V$, with content only for slot operators fixed in advance.

proofs.main:
\emph{Notation.} Numbers are read in $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$ (conventions); $D$ is the slot doublet, $F = \Lambda^{\bullet}D$, $V = F \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}W$; $a_{i} = a(u_{i}) \otimes 1$ ($u_{1}, u_{2}$ an orthonormal basis of $D$, $a^{\dagger}(u) = u \wedge$), $b_{p} = 1 \otimes b(t_{p})$ ($t_{1}, t_{2}, t_{3}$ an orthonormal basis of $W$), $(-1)^{k} = 1 \otimes (-1)^{\deg}$ the pair parity, $(-1)^{N} = (-1)^{n}(-1)^{k}$, and $\tilde a_{i} = a_{i}(-1)^{k}$. Products of operators on a tensor product: $(X \otimes Y)(X' \otimes Y') = XX' \otimes YY'$, so operators on different factors commute.

\emph{Step 1 (realisation in geometric algebra).} Take the floor $\Cl(5,5)$ of \claimref{synthesis.even-slots-need-a-spectator-generator}: generators $e_{k}$ ($e_{k}^{2} = 1$), $f_{k}$ ($f_{k}^{2} = -1$), $k = 0, \dots, 4$, null pairs $v_{k} = \tfrac12(e_{k} + f_{k})$, $w_{k} = \tfrac12(e_{k} - f_{k})$ with $v_{k}w_{l} + w_{l}v_{k} = \delta_{kl}$ and all other anticommutators zero, modes $0, 1$ the slots and $2, 3, 4$ the pairs, vacuum the null blade $\Omega = w_{0}\cdots w_{4}$. The $32$ states $v_{K}v_{J}\Omega$ ($v_{K}$ an ordered product of pair creators, $v_{J}$ of slot creators) are independent and span the Fock ideal; identify $v_{K}v_{J}\Omega$ with $u_{J} \otimes t_{K}$. A pair vector, acting from the left, passes no slot vector, so it acts as $1 \otimes b$; a slot vector passes the $k$ pair creators of $v_{K}$, so it acts as $a \otimes (-1)^{k}$: the vectors $v_{i}, w_{i}$ ($i = 0, 1$) are the twisted $\tilde a^{\dagger}_{i}, \tilde a_{i}$, and the untwisted ones are $v_{i}\Gamma_{W}$, $w_{i}\Gamma_{W}$ with $\Gamma_{W} = \prod_{p}(1 - 2v_{p}w_{p})$, the pair parity, as in clause (iii) of that result; the device is the commuting-copies twist of \claimref{tower.commuting-copies} read backwards. Since $2v_{p}w_{p} = \tfrac12(e_{p} + f_{p})(e_{p} - f_{p}) = 1 - e_{p}f_{p}$, $1 - 2v_{p}w_{p} = e_{p}f_{p}$ and $\Gamma_{W} = e_{2}f_{2}e_{3}f_{3}e_{4}f_{4}$ is a single blade, $\Gamma_{W}^{2} = 1$, commuting with the slot vectors and anticommuting with the six pair vectors. Over $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, $I_{4}$ commuting with all ten generators, $\Cl(5,5)$ spans $\mathrm{End}(V)$.

\emph{Step 2 ((i) and (ii)).} $\Gamma_{W}$ commutes with $a_{i}$, $a_{i}^{\dagger}$ and squares to $1$, so $\tilde a_{i}\tilde a_{j}^{\dagger} + \tilde a_{j}^{\dagger}\tilde a_{i} = a_{i}a_{j}^{\dagger} + a_{j}^{\dagger}a_{i} = \delta_{ij}$ and likewise for the other anticommutators. $A \otimes \Lambda^{\bullet}B$ preserves the pair degree, so it commutes with $(-1)^{k}$ and $\tilde a_{i}$ transforms as $a_{i}$ does. On $F_{n} \otimes \Lambda^{k}W$, $\tilde a_{i}^{\dagger} = (-1)^{k}a_{i}^{\dagger}$, so the creation maps have the same images and clause (G) holds for one set exactly when it holds for the other. The $a_{i}$ act on the first factor and the $b_{p}$ on the second, so they commute; $(-1)^{k}$ anticommutes with $b_{p}$ and $b_{p}^{\dagger}$, so $\tilde a_{i}b_{p} = -b_{p}\tilde a_{i}$ (in $\Cl(5,5)$: distinct vectors anticommute). Hence $\tilde a_{1}, \tilde a_{2}, b_{1}, b_{2}, b_{3}$ satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations of one system of five modes, and the real Majorana combinations $\tilde a + \tilde a^{\dagger}$, $\tilde a - \tilde a^{\dagger}$, $b + b^{\dagger}$, $b - b^{\dagger}$ are the ten vectors $e_{k}$, $f_{k}$, generating $\Cl(5,5)$; its span over $\mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$ is the $\Cl(10)$ of clause (f), with no imaginary unit needed for the Majorana of square $-1$.

\emph{Step 3 ((iii)).} For two slot operators $x, y$, $(x\Gamma_{W})(y\Gamma_{W}) = xy\,\Gamma_{W}^{2} = xy$; so every slot-slot bilinear, in particular the $\binom{4}{2} = 6$ slot Majorana bivectors, is the same element in both conventions. The pair operators are not twisted, so the $\binom{6}{2} = 15$ pair Majorana bivectors are the same too: the $21$ split-preserving bivectors of clause (CPT), the Pati-Salam algebra (\claimref{standard-model.automorphisms-preserve-slot-pair-split-are}, cited for the name only), do not depend on the convention. $\Gamma_{W}$ commutes with every slot-slot and pair-pair bilinear, the generators of $\uu(2) \oplus \uu(3)$ and the pair creation and annihilation bilinears among them. The grading $(-1)^{N} = \prod_{k=0}^{4}e_{k}f_{k}$ anticommutes with every one of the ten vectors and commutes with $\Gamma_{W}$, so it anticommutes with $a_{i}$, $\tilde a_{i}$ and $b_{p}$ alike: the grading form of clause (CPT) does not depend on the convention either.

\emph{Step 4 ((iv), uniqueness).} Let $K$ commute with every $a_{i}$, $a_{i}^{\dagger}$, and let $a_{i}K$ anticommute with every $b_{p}$, $b_{p}^{\dagger}$ and satisfy the canonical anticommutation relations. For a pair operator $\beta$, $a_{i}K\beta + \beta a_{i}K = a_{i}(K\beta + \beta K)$, and likewise with $a_{i}^{\dagger}$; adding $a_{i}^{\dagger}$ times the first to $a_{i}$ times the second gives $K\beta + \beta K = 0$. So $K(-1)^{k}$ commutes with every pair operator and every slot operator. The slot operators generate $\mathrm{End}(F) \otimes 1$ and the pair operators $1 \otimes \mathrm{End}(\Lambda^{\bullet}W)$ (the Fock representations of the canonical anticommutation relations are irreducible), which together generate $\mathrm{End}(V)$; so $K(-1)^{k}$ is a number $c \in \mathrm{span}\{1, I_{4}\}$, and the relation $(a_{i}K)(a_{i}K)^{\dagger} + (a_{i}K)^{\dagger}(a_{i}K) = |c|^{2} = 1$ makes $c$ a unit; $c = \pm 1$ when $K$ is an involution or a real element of the floor. A unit $c$ is a phase that the centre of the slot $U(2)$ already supplies. In the realisation the same follows by counting blades with the commutation form of \claimref{synthesis.blade-square-signs-f2-quadratic-form}(ii): blades $e_{S}$, $e_{T}$ anticommute exactly when $b(S, T) = |S||T| + |S \cap T| = 1 \pmod 2$; the conditions are diagonal in the blade basis, and with $P = \{e_{2}, e_{3}, e_{4}, f_{2}, f_{3}, f_{4}\}$, $b(S, \{x\}) = |S| + [x \in S] = 1$ for all $x \in P$ forces $S \supseteq P$ with $|S|$ even or $S \cap P = \emptyset$ with $|S|$ odd, and commuting with the untwisted slot Majoranas $e_{S'}$, $S' = \{y\} \cup P$, forces $[y \in S] = |S| + |S \cap P| \pmod 2$ for the four slot generators $y$; the first case gives $S = P$, the second would need all four slot generators in $S$ with $|S| = 4$ odd. So $K \in \mathrm{span}\{\Gamma_{W}\}$.

\emph{Step 5 (the reading; (v)).} By Steps 2 to 4, on $V$ the operators required by clause (f) exist whenever $F \cong \Lambda^{\bullet}D$, namely the Klein-twisted slot operators, unique up to a unit; every operator the clause produces ($\Cl(10)$, $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$, the $24$ cross bivectors) is an operator on $V$ built from them, and everything clause (CPT) asks of the convention is convention-free. The $24$ cross bivectors do depend on the convention (only the twisted operators give $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$); the residual sign $c = -1$ acts on them by $\mathrm{Ad}$ of the slot parity $(-1)^{n} = e_{0}f_{0}e_{1}f_{1}$ (of reverse norm $1$, the central element $-1$ of the slot $U(2)$, an element of $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$), which negates the slot Majoranas and fixes the pair ones, so the $\mathrm{Spin}(10)$ of clause (f) is canonical as a subgroup. So on $V$ clause (f) is a choice of convention with no content of its own. It keeps content only relative to an embedding of slot operators given in advance, for instance as tower elements, where the question is whether the given operators are the twisted or the untwisted ones; this is the setting of \claimref{synthesis.even-slots-need-a-spectator-generator}(iii), which already makes the replacement $s_{i} \mapsto s_{i}\Gamma_{W}$, and it is not addressed here. The checks verify Steps 1 to 4 exactly in $\Cl(5,5)$, including the commutation form against the products for all $1024$ blades.
